html:
The Alutiiq, or Sugpiaq, are a coastal Alaska Native people of Kodiak Island, the Alaska Peninsula, Prince William Sound and the Kenai Peninsula. They speak Alutiiq, a Yupik language related to that of the Yup'ik.

They lived in large sod houses and hunted sea mammals from skin kayaks with finely made harpoons; their ancestors have lived on Kodiak for about 7,500 years. In 1784 the Russian fur trader Grigory Shelikhov attacked the Sugpiaq at Refuge Rock near Three Saints Bay, killing many, and founded the first Russian settlement in Alaska. Under the Russian-American Company Alutiiq men were forced to hunt sea otters across the North Pacific.

In 1964 the Good Friday earthquake and its tsunami destroyed several of their villages. See Russian America and the Aleut, with whom the Russians often grouped them.
